clue.text: Cloudless section distinct

blocks.note: a cloudless sky is a clear one
a cut is a section, as of meat

explanation.surface: A weather report: one part of the sky stands out as clear of cloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Something clear-cut is sharply defined and unambiguous, a synonym for distinct.

clue.text: One about to leave republic to top the bill with another

definitions.text: to top the bill with another

indicators.note: what leaves departs, so those letters are taken away from the rest

blocks.note: Costa Rica is a Central American republic
I is the Roman numeral for one
ca, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A political exile is about to quit the republic and share top billing elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The I and the CA come off the end of the country's name, leaving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To co-star is to share the leading billing in a film or play with another performer.

clue.text: Cake Alice baked right

indicators.note: baking transforms raw ingredients, so the letters are mixed into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Alice got her baking just right and produced a fine cake.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a finger of choux pastry filled with cream, a kind of small cake.

clue.text: Much associated with this outlaw

blocks.note: surface reading: an outlaw with a great many associations
setter's reading: Much the Miller's Son, one of the Merry Men in the Sherwood legend

explanation.walkthrough: 'Much' looks like a quantity word; capitalised by its position, it is the name of a member of the outlaw's band.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sherwood Forest outlaw of English legend led a band including Little John, Friar Tuck and Much.

clue.text: Surely incorrect to include companion, but easy to understand

indicators.note: an incorrect arrangement is a wrong one, so the letters are set in another order
including something puts it inside the rest

blocks.note: taken as written
a friend is a companion

explanation.surface: Insisting a pal be included is surely wrong, though the reasoning is easy enough to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Software or instructions described as user-friendly are simple for ordinary people to grasp and operate.

clue.text: A copper confronting servants demonstrates intuition

indicators.note: to confront is to stand face to face, so the first part is set directly before the next

blocks.note: taken as written
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
men in the old sense of manservants

explanation.surface: A police officer facing down the household staff shows a detective's instinct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' invites a policeman, which suits the surface; here it is the metal, by its chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Acumen is keen insight or shrewd judgement, close enough in sense to intuition.

clue.text: Church member's appeal

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A church member makes a heartfelt appeal for funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests a congregant; here it is a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: Charm is the power to attract or delight, which is what appeal means as a noun.

clue.text: Male duck exposes poisonous plant

blocks.note: a man is a male
a drake is a male duck

explanation.surface: A drake on the pond turns up a toxic weed.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandrake is a Mediterranean plant of the nightshade family whose forked root is toxic.

clue.text: You'll find my charges low!

blocks.note: surface reading: a tradesman boasting of cheap prices
setter's reading: the animals in my charge moo, so the speaker looks after cattle

explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' is the verb for what cattle do, and 'charges' are the creatures someone tends, not fees.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat is an old word for cattle, so the answer is an archaic term for a cowherd.

clue.text: Preserved meat - sailor's to complain

blocks.note: an old salt is an experienced sailor
to beef is slang for to grumble

explanation.surface: Salted rations on board give a sailor something to grumble about.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt beef is beef cured in brine, a classic preserved meat of ships' stores.

clue.text: Iran, an amazing magical land

indicators.note: something amazing leaves you bewildered, so the letters are thrown into confusion

blocks.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Praise for Iran as a wonderful, almost enchanted country.
explanation.definitionFit: Narnia is the enchanted kingdom of C. S. Lewis's children's novels, a fictional magical realm.

clue.text: Fruit began to go off in trucks

indicators.note: food that goes off spoils, so the letters are spoilt into a new order
in places one part inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
lorry is the British word for a truck

explanation.surface: A load of fruit started to rot while it sat in the lorries.
explanation.definitionFit: Loganberries are dark red berries from a cross between a raspberry and a blackberry.

clue.text: Story swallowed by an immigrant

indicators.note: what is swallowed ends up inside the one that swallows it

blocks.note: taken as written
a story is a fib or untruth

explanation.surface: A tale believed wholesale by a newcomer to the country.
explanation.definitionFit: An alien is a foreign national living in a country, an official word for an immigrant.

clue.text: Force someone to move from vault, gallons having been imbibed

indicators.note: a drink that is imbibed goes inside the drinker

blocks.note: taken as written
a vault is an arched roof
G is the abbreviation for gallons

explanation.surface: Drunks, gallons inside them, being hustled out from under the cellar vault.
explanation.walkthrough: The G goes inside the word from, between its O and M, and the vault follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To frogmarch is to propel a person forward by holding their arms from behind, forcing them along.

clue.text: Singer Billie's producer, one on a tour?

blocks.note: Billie Holiday was the American jazz singer
a maker produces things

explanation.surface: A question about the record producer who worked with Billie Holiday on tour.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a tourist is only one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A holidaymaker is a person away on vacation, and a tourist on a tour is one such traveller.

clue.text: Girl in factory, one on little money

blocks.note: a mill is a factory
I is the Roman numeral for one
a cent is a small coin

explanation.surface: A mill girl at the factory, working for next to nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Millicent is a female given name, and crosswords often define a name simply as girl.

clue.text: A party overcomes tricky point in formal selection of candidate?

indicators.note: something tricky is awkward and twisted, so the letters are turned around
in a down answer, what overcomes another sits on top of it

blocks.note: taken as written
a do is a party
taken as written

explanation.surface: A political party gets past an awkward procedural point in choosing its candidate.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests elections, but the question mark hints that the candidate is a child taken into a family.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoption is the legal process of choosing to take a child as one's own, or formally choosing a party nominee.

clue.text: Song about a lamia, ultimately an object of loathing

indicators.note: about means around, so one part surrounds another
ultimately points to what comes at the very end of the word

blocks.note: an anthem is a song
taken as written
final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A song about a lamia, a mythical female monster, which ends up hated.
explanation.walkthrough: A lamia is a mythical monster, half woman and half serpent; only its last letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is anathema to a person is intensely detested, a thing they loathe.

clue.text: Fight ring in nursery rhyme

blocks.note: a ding-dong is a heated argument or scrap
to give someone a bell is to ring them; a bell rings

explanation.surface: A boxing bout in the ring, oddly found inside a children's verse.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Ding, Dong, Bell, Pussy's in the well' is a traditional children's rhyme.

clue.text: Shortly extra beer will bring confidence

indicators.note: cut short, the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: more means extra
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Another pint before long will give you Dutch courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Morale is the confidence and spirit of a person or group, as in team morale.

clue.text: Very bad cut on base of spine

indicators.note: in a down entry the base of a word is its bottom, final letter

blocks.note: to sever is to cut
final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A medical note: a nasty gash at the bottom of the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe describes something serious or intense, as a severe injury is a very bad one.

clue.text: Work of little merit in vessel, British tanker

blocks.note: a pot is a cooking vessel
B is the abbreviation for British
an oiler is a ship that carries oil

explanation.surface: A shipping report: a British oil tanker among the vessels at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A potboiler is a book written quickly for money, so a piece of hack work of little literary value.

clue.text: Clean bracing air round region

blocks.note: O is round in shape
a zone is a region

explanation.surface: Fresh sea air surrounding a whole area.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is used loosely, especially in Britain, for fresh invigorating seaside air.

clue.text: United at home against last in league

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: being in means being at home
as in leaning on, that is against, a wall
final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Manchester United, playing at home, face the bottom club in the league.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like a football team, which the league supports; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Things combined in one are joined together into a single whole, hence united.

clue.text: Diamonds put by carton in fridge compartment

blocks.note: ice is slang for diamonds
a carton is a cardboard box

explanation.surface: A jewel thief stashing the diamonds in a carton hidden in the fridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The icebox is the freezing section at the top of an older refrigerator.

clue.text: Learned to repeat after foremost of lecturers

indicators.note: the foremost part of a word is its opening letter
coming after means the next part is placed behind the earlier one

blocks.note: opening letter of the word
to iterate is to repeat

explanation.surface: A student learnt by parroting back what the leading lecturers said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Learned' reads as a past-tense verb, but it is the adjective meaning well read.
explanation.definitionFit: Literate means well educated or well read, the sense of learned as an adjective.

clue.text: Approached miserly editor

blocks.note: near is an old word for stingy
ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A tight-fisted editor is approached, perhaps for a pay rise.
explanation.definitionFit: To have neared something is to have drawn close to it, a synonym for approached.

clue.text: Sweatier in resort, so to speak

indicators.note: read resort as re-sort, sorting the letters into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers get hotter and stickier at a seaside resort, so to say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday town; split as re-sort it tells you to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are idioms softening a statement, signalling that the words are used loosely or figuratively.
